conventions: A preposition on an absolute noun that the ASV recasts as a single English word fuses with that noun under rules 30 and 40 even where the word is a predicate adjective rather than the adverb rule 40's examples name: בְּעֹז renders is strong (24.5) as one unit headed on עֹז, with the construction-supplied copula joining that fused unit under rules 20 and 49, and בַּחוּץ renders without (24.27) on the same terms. Do not mark the preposition unrepresented beside a noun holding the whole rendering, and do not read the margin's literal gloss (Hebrew is in strength) as writing an in the printed text does not have (rule 38). An article morpheme standing in such a phrase is no part of the fusion: it takes a written the where one is written and is unrepresented where none is (24.5, 24.27).

Where the ASV converts a Hebrew rhetorical question into an English prohibition, the interrogative particle is unrepresented under rule 17's inversion sentence and the English negative belongs to the prohibitive אַל standing at the head of the coordinated first colon under rule 25's distribution, not to the הֲ whose rhetorical force the recasting has consumed: וְהֲפִתִּיתָ בִּשְׂפָתֶיךָ renders And deceive not with thy lips (24.28), the second not going to the אַל of Be not a witness. Rule 25's distribution is read over more than two cola where the Hebrew writes the particle once: 24.12 carries one הֲ and one לֹא across three coordinated clauses, taking Doth ... doth ... shall and three nots, each headed on the first occurrence.

Where a colon writes both a participle or substantive needing an English noun phrase and an explicit resumptive pronoun, count the ASV's pronouns against the two morphemes before placing them (rule 42's counting reasoning). PRO.24.12 writes one he in the first colon, which goes to the explicit הוּא while the participle keeps only the supplied that, and two hes in the second, where the participle takes he that under rule 46 and the הוּא takes the second he. One verse writes both shapes; the competing reading, giving he that to the participle and marking הוּא unrepresented, is named in that verse's notes.
report: Read all 40 candidate lemma groups and then the whole verse dump end to end, since the table is keyed by source lemma and is blind to added units. No cross-verse split found; patches empty.

Every multi-treatment bucket is licensed by the source or by what the ASV wrote. אַל rendered Neither at 24.19 stands in a colon with no waw in it (rule 35's lone negative), while 24.1's Neither fuses a waw that is written. הֲ takes the fronted auxiliary at 24.12 and is unrepresented at 24.28, where the ASV recast the rhetorical question as a prohibition and wrote no auxiliary. לְ with a 3ms suffix is unrepresented at 24.8 (bare English object, rule 40) and takes to at 24.29, where a to is written. Td before Vhrmpa takes them that at 24.25 under rule 41 and nothing at 24.19, where the ASV writes evil doers with no determiner and no relative.

The two retribution formulas — הֵשִׁיב לְאָדָם כְּפָעֳלוֹ (24.12) and אָשִׁיב לָאִישׁ כְּפָעֳלוֹ (24.29) — are aligned identically: לְ to to, כְּ to according to headed on according, construct noun work, suffix his. That agrees with the corpus, which heads according to on according in 113 לְ units and 45 בְּ units.

Checked the dimensions the table cannot see. Supplied definite and indefinite determiners join their nominal in every occurrence and are never added. Supplied subject pronouns always join their finite verb (rule 17). Supplied lexical subjects and verbs are consistently added — Men (24.8), see (24.11), sayings (24.23) — while generics completing a substantive are consistently folded — man (24.15, 24.16, 24.20), times (24.16), doers (24.19). Supplied object pronouns are added in all six places (24.12 twice, 24.14, 24.18, 24.22, 24.25). Supplied prepositions reaching a bare complement go to the verb in all four (24.2 talk of, 24.4 are filled With, 24.23 have respect of, 24.31 grown over with and covered with).

Phrasal particles pass rule 44's subtraction the same way throughout: away, back, out and down stay with carried away, hold back, put out, turn away and broken down, because the bare English verb does not write the source lexeme in any of those; and 24.16's again is added because riseth up has already written קוּם. That is one test applied consistently, not two treatments.

Supplied connectives are treated alike wherever no conjunction morpheme stands in the clause: If (24.10), And (24.21), two ands (24.32), Yet (24.33) are each added under rules 14 and 55, while every colon that does write a waw gives it the connective the ASV wrote, including the And of And afterwards at 24.27, where the adverb takes its own word under rule 14's closing paragraph.

BSB: none of the five disagreements is an error. 24.6 לְּ and 24.8 לוֹ are rule 40 recastings (a possessive determiner on the noun beside it; a bare English object). 24.14 ה is a paragogic he, the case rule 32 names as the bulk of the BSB difference. 24.28 הֲ is the question-to-prohibition recasting, corroborated by the edition's own literal gloss. 24.32 י stands outside the שִׁית לֵב fusion and the ASV writes no my anywhere in considered well. All five are documented convention differences; no accepted edge was changed.

Promotions: none. The one judgment that looked general — that a בְּ plus absolute noun recast as a single English word fuses under rules 30 and 40 even when that word is an adjective rather than the adverb rule 40 names — is recorded as a convention instead, because the corpus extract for בְּ reports 720 unrepresented units without a breakdown and I cannot confirm from it that the corpus does not read that shape the other way. A rule the corpus contradicts is worse than none, so it stays chapter-scoped.
